effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` PYUSD to the vault (safeTransferFrom msg.sender to vault).
The vault mints previewDeposit(assets) senPYUSDmWIN shares to `onBehalf`; the share amount comes from the stored share price.
formats.shown: Deposit {assets} PYUSD for {onBehalf}, with the share ticker senPYUSDmWIN and the share recipient as fields.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many shares the signer receives; the amount comes from the stored share price
findings.evidence: VaultV2.deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The descriptor has only the constant field 'Share ticker' = senPYUSDmWIN. In case 0 the signer received 2000000000000000000 senPYUSDmWIN and the screen shows no amount.
findings.fix: No descriptor fix exists, because the share amount is not in calldata and the function has no minimum-shares parameter.

cases.notes: The screen shows the 2 PYUSD out correctly. For the shares in, it shows the ticker and the recipient (the signer) but no amount, so the reader's understanding is partial.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns previewWithdraw(assets) senPYUSDmWIN shares from `onBehalf`; the share amount comes from the stored price and has no maximum.
If msg.sender is not onBehalf, the call spends that many shares of the owner's allowance to the signer.
The vault sends exactly `assets` PYUSD to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly {assets} PYUSD to {receiver}, with an Owner field; nothing mentions the vault shares that are burned.

findings.title: withdraw never states that senPYUSDmWIN shares are burned from the owner
findings.evidence: VaultV2.exit: `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares);`. The descriptor has the intent 'Withdraw', the sentence 'Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver}', and no share field. In case 2 the signer gave 999601107758894293 senPYUSDmWIN, and the reader wrote 'Possibly a vault share/position token ... (screen doesn't say)'.
findings.fix: Add a constant field {"label":"Shares burned","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker"}. Change interpolatedIntent to 'Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver} by burning senPYUSDmWIN shares'.

findings.title: withdraw cannot show the number of shares burned; previewWithdraw computes it from storage
findings.evidence: VaultV2.withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);`. The calldata has no maxShares parameter.

cases.notes: The screen shows the 1 PYUSD in correctly. It does not show the shares out, and the reader only guessed at them.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` senPYUSDmWIN from `onBehalf`; if msg.sender is not onBehalf, the call spends the owner's allowance to the signer.
The vault sends previewRedeem(shares) PYUSD to `receiver`; the amount comes from the stored price and has no minimum.
formats.shown: Redeem {shares} senPYUSDmWIN to {receiver}, with an Owner field; the screen never names the asset received or its amount.

findings.title: redeem never names PYUSD as the asset the receiver gets
findings.evidence: VaultV2.exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);`. The redeem fields are only 'Shares to redeem', 'To' and 'Owner'. In case 3 the signer received 1700028778288 PYUSD, and the reader wrote 'Underlying asset (likely PYUSD, based on the name) ... amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Add {"label":"Receive asset","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"}, as the mint format does. Change interpolatedIntent to 'Redeem {#.shares} for PYUSD to {#.receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem cannot show the PYUSD amount received; previewRedeem computes it from storage
findings.evidence: VaultV2.redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. The calldata has no minAssets parameter.

cases.notes: The screen shows the shares out exactly. The reader only guessed the PYUSD in, from the vault name, and saw no amount.

effects: The signer sends previewMint(shares) PYUSD to the vault; the amount comes from the stored price and has no maximum.
The vault mints exactly `shares` senPYUSDmWIN to `onBehalf`.
formats.shown: Mint {shares} senPYUSDmWIN for {onBehalf}, with a 'Deposit asset: PYUSD' field that has no amount.

findings.title: mint's intent and sentence do not say that PYUSD leaves the signer's wallet
findings.evidence: VaultV2.enter: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets);`. The descriptor has the intent 'Mint' and the sentence 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. In case 1 the signer paid 1000000 PYUSD, and the summary line does not mention it.
findings.fix: Change the intent to 'Deposit PYUSD to mint shares'. Change interpolatedIntent to 'Deposit PYUSD to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

findings.title: mint cannot show the PYUSD amount taken; previewMint computes it from storage with no cap
findings.evidence: VaultV2.mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The screen field 'Deposit asset' shows 'PYUSD' with no amount. Case 1 took 1000000 PYUSD.

cases.notes: The screen names PYUSD as the deposit asset but gives no amount. The shares went to 0xdead, which is not the signer, and the screen shows that correctly.
